item.title: New Albany and Union County students finish the fall term on different days
item.description: Families getting ready for the return from Thanksgiving can plan for two different December school schedules in Union County, Mississippi. New Albany School District ends the nine-week grading period Friday, December 11. Its final student day before the holiday is Thursday, December 17, a 60% day. Friday, December 18 is a professional development day in the city district. Union County School District students attend through Friday, December 18. That is both their 60% day and the end of their nine-week grading period. The county district explicitly lists Monday, November 30 as its return from Thanksgiving break. Both official calendars mark November 23–27 as the holiday. Neither annual calendar gives a campus dismissal clock time for a 60% day. Both districts set Monday, January 4 for staff professional development. Students in both districts return Tuesday, January 5 and receive report cards Friday, January 8. New Albany official 2026–27 calendar: https://www.newalbanyschools.us/PDF/calendar27.pdf . Union County board-approved calendar: https://content.myconnectsuite.com/api/documents/1c9669e88956468c8d012be0b8586018 . County district return notice and calendar download: https://www.union.k12.ms.us/ .
item.source: New Albany School District and Union County School District

item.title: Severe drought holds across four-fifths of Union County
item.description: The November 24 table puts 80.16% of Union County, which includes New Albany, in severe drought or worse. The 2.28% in extreme drought is included in the 80.16%. No area reached exceptional drought. The remaining 19.84% was moderately dry. The severe-or-worse share held steady from November 17 after rising from 20.45% on November 10. On November 10, 1.13% of the county was extreme or worse. The percentages are shares of land area. Categories in the U.S. Drought Monitor table are cumulative; the more severe categories are included in the less severe ones. The national map is dated Tuesday, November 24, before Wednesday’s weather. The map does not measure subsequent rainfall. Statewide, extreme drought or worse covered 66.91% of Mississippi on November 24, up from 53.56% the week before. Sources: https://usdmdataservices.unl.edu/api/CountyStatistics/GetDroughtSeverityStatisticsByAreaPercent?aoi=28145&startdate=11/10/2026&enddate=11/24/2026&statisticsType=1 (county area percentages for November 10, 17 and 24); https://droughtmonitor.unl.edu/data/png/20261124/20261124_ms_text.png (dated state map and statewide comparison).

item.title: Union County voters choose between Adams and Byers in Dec. 1 judicial runoff
item.description: Union County voters will choose between Bart M. Adams and Shirley C. Byers for Circuit Court District 3, Place 2, in the Tuesday, Dec. 1, 2026 nonpartisan judicial runoff. The state sample ballot lists both candidates. The Mississippi judicial directory names Union County as one of the seven counties in the Third Circuit Court District. The sample ballot combines different districts statewide; voters can use their home address in the state My Election Day portal to see their own ballot and polling place. In a Nov. 24 notice, the Mississippi Secretary of State set out deadlines. People eligible to vote absentee in person have a final Saturday window on Nov. 28 from 8 a.m. to noon at their circuit clerk’s office, according to the state’s absentee notice. The Union County circuit clerk is Donna Treadaway in New Albany. The state court directory lists her office number as 662-534-1910. On Tuesday, Dec. 1, polls open at 7 a.m. and close at 7 p.m. Voters already in line at 7 p.m. may still vote. A mailed absentee ballot must be postmarked by Dec. 1 and received by the circuit clerk by Dec. 8. For a voter who casts an affidavit ballot after forgetting photo ID, the deadline to present acceptable identification at the circuit clerk’s office is also Dec. 8. Sources: https://www.sos.ms.gov/news/election-day-reminders-2026-general-runoff-election (Nov. 24 election reminders); https://www.sos.ms.gov/content/documents/Elections/2026/Run%20Off%20Sample%20Ballot%2012-1-2026.pdf (page two, District 03 Place 2); https://www.sos.ms.gov/sites/default/files/publications/Circuit%20Court%20and%20Terms%202026.pdf (Third Circuit counties); https://www.sos.ms.gov/news/saturday-person-absentee-voting-begins-upcoming-deadlines-2026-general-runoff-election (Saturday hours); https://www.courts.ms.gov/trialcourts/circuitcourt/circuitclerks.pdf (Union County clerk); https://myelectionday.sos.state.ms.us/VoterOutreach/Pages/VOSearch.aspx (address-specific ballot and polling place).

item.title: New Albany parade groups need one QR pass per entry for Monday check-in
item.description: The New Albany Main Street Association has issued instructions for groups already registered for the New Albany and Union County Christmas Parade on Monday, November 30, 2026. Its entry confirmation identifies the Tallahatchie Trail staging area and instructs the contact for each registered entry to have the QR check-in pass ready for volunteers to scan. One pass covers the entire parade entry, regardless of how many people ride or walk with that group. Staging begins at 3 p.m. The downtown parade begins at 6:30 p.m. The pass is for the parade lineup. Each organization designates somebody to handle its application and share instructions with the group. The Main Street guidelines say band directors or their designated contacts receive separate arrival and staging instructions. Families accompanying band students should follow those directions. The route passes beneath the Tanglefoot Trail bicycle bridge on Main Street. The bridge has 14 feet of clearance. Main Street asks that vehicles, floats, trailers and their decorations measure no more than 13 feet high from the ground. Organizers may arrange for taller entries to leave the route before reaching the bridge. Tractor-trailers cannot use the regular staging area. The entry confirmation lists the Main Street office at 662-534-3438 for questions. https://www.newalbanymainstreet.com/2026parade

item.title: Union County unemployment rises to 3.1% in October
item.description: Union County, Mississippi, including New Albany. The October 2026 preliminary residence-based estimates in the Mississippi Department of Employment Security report put the local unemployment rate at 3.1% in October after a revised 2.7% in September. The August rate was 2.5%. The department counts 12,803 county residents in the October civilian labor force. Of them 12,410 were employed and 393 were unemployed. In September the labor force numbered 12,827, with 12,477 employed and 350 unemployed. The unemployed total rose by 43 residents. The employed count fell by 67. The change in the civilian labor force was -24 people. The survey describes people age 16 and older by where they live. A resident who commutes outside the county remains part of the county residence-based estimates. These counts should not be described as employers adding or eliminating positions. The number unemployed and the number employed together equal the civilian labor force in each month. The comparable Mississippi rate was 3.6%, based on 45,914 unemployed and 1,214,626 employed residents in a civilian labor force of 1,260,540. Both state and county figures in this comparison are unadjusted for seasonal changes. A separate county table in the same release lists 26 initial unemployment insurance claims and 128 continued claims in October compared with 15 initial and 153 continued claims in September. Insurance claims are an administrative measure. They should not be added together or treated as the number of unemployed residents. September is revised and October is preliminary. The tables do not establish what caused any change. The department’s county series gives these monthly rates earlier in 2026: June at 3.3%, July at 3.0%, August at 2.5%, September at 2.7%, October at 3.1%. Source documents: https://mdes.ms.gov/media/23357/labormarketdata.pdf (labor force estimates and county unemployment insurance claims); https://mdes.ms.gov/media/8735/urate.pdf (county monthly unemployment series); https://mdes.ms.gov/media/8654/uratesmapbw.pdf (October county unemployment rate map).

item.title: New Albany Middle School and New Albany’s career school appear on TVA classroom award roster
item.description: New Albany Middle School — New Albany Light Water and Gas. New Albany School of Career and Technical Education — New Albany Light Water and Gas. TVA's workbook names New Albany Middle School and New Albany School of Career and Technical Education under the utility New Albany Light Water and Gas. Another entry under that same utility is printed simply as School of Career and Technical Education, without a place name. Its identity is unresolved. Report the two named New Albany schools without assigning the extra row to a separate campus or calculating a local total. The district identifies the New Albany School of Career and Technical Education as being on the New Albany High School campus. Its site describes twelve programs and more than 500 part-time students. Its regular programs include automotive service, construction, computer science and engineering, and engineering. The roster does not designate any of those programs as an award-funded project. The Tennessee Valley Authority and Bicentennial Volunteers, Inc., its retiree organization, announced the regional awards on November 23, 2026. The 2026–27 list contains 334 school entries across the region, 36 in TVA's Mississippi district. The program awards $1.5 million regionwide and TVA estimates about 96,000 students will benefit across the region. The $5,000 figure is an upper limit for an individual award. It is not the amount awarded to a named school. Eligible schools receive electricity through a local power company served by TVA. The competitive process gives preference to proposals dealing with the environment, energy, economic development or solving community problems. The Tennessee STEM Innovation Network is a program partner and Battelle manages the network. TVA says that since 2018 the partners have provided more than $10.5 million through these awards, supporting more than 940,000 students across the region. Primary award announcement: https://www.tva.com/the-powerhouse/stories/tva-awards--1.5-million-to-support-stem-education-across-the-valley_edu Award program and full recipient list: https://www.tva.com/learn/stem-awards Official workbook: https://tva-azr-eastus-cdn-ep-tvawcm-prd.azureedge.net/cdn-tvawcma/docs/default-source/tva-stem/2026--2027-tva-stem-award.xlsx?sfvrsn=87e985be_1 School district sources: https://www.newalbanyschools.us/, https://nahighschool.com/tech/
